$comment: Fuel catalog v0.1 (spec §8.5). Values taken VERBATIM from docs/research-notes.md §4 with their source_id, basis and original unit. Primary source: UK DESNZ 2025 (uk-desnz-ghg-2025) — density + NCV/GCV both bases + CO2/CH4/N2O split. Global/rank fallback: IPCC 2006 (ipcc-2006-v2) for crude oil, anthracite, lignite. NOTE ON UNITS: DESNZ publishes gravimetric energy as GJ/tonne, which is numerically identical to MJ/kg (1 GJ/tonne = 1 MJ/kg) — stored as mj_per_kg with the GJ/tonne origin noted, no silent conversion. Per-litre / per-m³ figures are DESNZ's own kWh/L, kWh/m³ (Net/Gross CV) columns. IPCC NCVs in TJ/Gg = GJ/tonne = MJ/kg. Missing properties are OMITTED (UI shows 'not available') — never invented (rulebook, AGENTS.md). Every heating_value carries basis + >=1 source_refs; density carries >=1 source_refs. See src/lib/data/schemas.ts (fuelSchema).

heating_values.notes: IPCC's 2006 guidelines (Vol. 2, Ch. 1, Table 1.2) list a global default net calorific value (NCV, or lower heating value/LHV) for crude oil of 42.3 MJ/kg (42.3 GJ/tonne), with a 95% confidence range of 40.1–44.8 MJ/kg. DESNZ's 2025 dataset has no generic 'crude oil' entry — it only covers refined products — so this IPCC figure is used here.

fuels.typical_ranges: Physical crude density varies by grade (~800–950 kg/m³, light vs heavy); a serious primary density was NOT FOUND in this pass, so density is omitted. Energy per physical barrel is an estimate (~5.6–6.3 GJ) and is NOT the same as 'boe' (fixed 5.8 MMBTU convention).
fuels.notes: This is a generic crude oil figure, based on IPCC 2006 global default values; there is no matching DESNZ entry. Density is deliberately left out, because we could not find it in a reliable primary source, so volume-to-mass conversions show 'not available' instead of a made-up number.
warnings: Crude oil is not a single substance: density and energy content vary by grade (API gravity). Any barrel↔energy or volume↔mass figure for crude is an ESTIMATE, not a measured property of a specific oil.
A physical barrel of crude is NOT the same as 'boe' (barrel of oil equivalent), which is a fixed 5.8 MMBTU energy-equivalence convention.

This is NOT how a gas bill is calculated: billing uses your supplier's local calorific value (Brennwert) and a state-correction number (Zustandszahl) that maps your meter's operating-condition m³ to reference energy. Do not use this result for billing disputes.

density.notes: Gas density is 0.08988 kg/m³ at standard temperature and pressure (STP: 0 °C, 1 atmosphere). Liquid hydrogen at its boiling point (−252.87 °C) is about 70.8 kg/m³, but that is not used as the primary figure here, since hydrogen is normally handled by mass rather than volume. Source: h2tools, cross-checked against other references.

heating_values.notes: LHV 119.96 MJ/kg (≈ 33.3 kWh/kg). h2tools / DOE-derived, cross-source-verified (primary page returned HTTP 403 on automated fetch; re-checked by follow-up).

HHV 141.79 MJ/kg (≈ 39.4 kWh/kg), NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69)-traceable printed value (285.83 kJ/mol). The DOE GREET/ORNL table gives 142.18 MJ/kg (gaseous) — hence the range. Earlier project figure 141.88 was between these; corrected to the NIST-printed 141.79. The LHV/HHV gap is large for hydrogen (~18%) because all combustion product is water.

fuels.notes: Hydrogen physical properties. Direct combustion CO2 = 0 (no carbon in the molecule) — handled by the engine as an exact physical fact, NOT via an emission factor. NOT FOUND in DESNZ 2025 or IPCC 2006 (both are fossil/biomass-scoped). No upstream/production emission factor is included in v0.1 (grey/blue/green H2 differ enormously) — upstream is out of scope and must NOT be implied as zero.
warnings: Direct combustion of hydrogen emits no CO2 (no carbon), but this is a COMBUSTION-ONLY figure. Upstream production emissions are NOT zero and depend entirely on the pathway (grey/SMR vs blue vs green) — they are not included here.
Hydrogen's LHV and HHV differ by ~18% — always check which basis a hydrogen energy figure uses.

No density is given by DESNZ (coal is sold by mass) → volume↔mass shows 'not available'. IPCC 2006 Other Bituminous Coal NCV 25.8 MJ/kg, CO2 94,600 kg/TJ. heating_values.notes: IPCC's 2006 guidelines (Vol. 2, Ch. 1, Table 1.2) list a global default net calorific value (NCV) for lignite of 11.9 MJ/kg (11.9 GJ/tonne), on a net basis, with a 95% confidence range of 5.50–21.6 MJ/kg — a very wide range, reflecting how much lignite's moisture and ash content can vary. DESNZ's 2025 dataset has no 'lignite' entry, so this IPCC figure is used here.

fuels.notes: Lignite (brown coal) uses the IPCC's 2006 global default figures. DESNZ groups coal by how it's used rather than by geological rank, so we use the IPCC's rank-based tables (Table 1.2 for calorific value, Table 2.2 for emissions) instead. No density is given in the source, so volume conversions are not available. The IPCC table only provides a net calorific value (NCV), not a higher heating value (HHV, also called gross calorific value or GCV), so that figure is shown as 'not available' too.
warnings: Lignite is extremely variable (moisture/ash): the IPCC net calorific value has a 95% range of 5.5–21.6 MJ/kg. Treat any lignite energy figure as a rough estimate. No density available → volume conversions not available.

heating_values.notes: IPCC's 2006 guidelines (Vol. 2, Ch. 1, Table 1.2) list a global default net calorific value (NCV) for anthracite of 26.7 MJ/kg (26.7 GJ/tonne), on a net basis, with a 95% confidence range of 21.6–32.2 MJ/kg. DESNZ's 2025 dataset has no 'anthracite' entry, so this IPCC figure is used here.

fuels.notes: Anthracite, IPCC 2006 global default (rank-based). DESNZ has no rank-based term. No density in the source → volume conversions not available. HHV/GCV not available from IPCC Table 1.2 (NCV only) → shows 'not available'.
warnings: No density available (coal is sold by mass) → volume conversions not available. HHV/GCV not available from the IPCC source used.

fuels.notes: Grid electricity is not a combustible material: it has no density or heating value, so mass and volume conversions simply do not apply (unlike a genuine data gap, which we mark 'not available'). '1 kWh of electricity' converts as pure energy (into kWh, MJ, BTU, etc., using exact SI conversions). We do not show a CO₂e figure until you choose a region and year, because grid carbon intensity depends on the country, the year, and even the time of day. The region/year figures shown (UK 2025, EU-27 2023, EU-27 2022) are illustrative examples, not global defaults — both EU years are shown together on purpose, to make clear how much grid intensity changes from year to year.
warnings: Grid electricity CO2e has no single correct global factor — it depends on the country/region, the year, and even the time of day. Pick a region and year for a real figure; the values shown without one are illustrative examples only, not defaults.
Illustrative region+year electricity factors are generation-only / location-based (see each factor's own uncertainty note) and are not updated in real time.
